labor-force.def: Everyone who is employed or unemployed. The labor force participation rate is the labor force divided by the adult population, times 100.

unemployment-rate.def: The percent of the labor force that is unemployed: unemployed divided by labor force, times 100. A person is unemployed if they have no job, are available and looked for work recently.

frictional.def: Unemployment while people search between jobs or enter the labor force, such as a nurse who moved and is applying for nursing jobs.

structural.def: Unemployment when workers' skills or locations do not match the jobs available, often after technology or the pattern of demand changes.

cyclical.def: Unemployment caused by a fall in total spending and output during a downturn; it equals the actual unemployment rate minus the natural rate.

natural-rate.def: The unemployment rate when cyclical unemployment is zero: frictional plus structural unemployment. When the actual rate equals it, the economy is at full employment.

discouraged.def: A person who wants a job but has stopped looking because they believe none is available. Discouraged workers are not in the labor force; underemployed workers have part-time jobs but want full-time ones.
